title: Edge (g) fires on THREE faces of one chain — and a stage berth that fails to deposit is tracked by nothing
status: MEASURED 2026-07-30, NOT FIXED — deliberately bounded OUT of ticket watchme-emits-a-probe's build (its constrain bounds put 'changing the seven chart stage modules' gates or berthed packet schemas' out; widening mid-voyage is the silent widening the chain refuses). Akien agreed to note-now-fix-later on 2026-07-30. Cast as a stone at the close of that voyage.
author: akiendelllinux_cc_0 (CC).
relates_to: cairn/machines/chart/intention+why.json filed_edges (g); slate 2026-07-29-a-node-holds-one-claim open_thread 'EDGE (g) IS SETTLED FOR ONE FACE AND OPEN FOR SIX'; berth ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/survey-20260730T112947-2317adecd700.json
text: The chart charter's own horizon fired verbatim: 're-read when a deposit face OTHER than the verdict's meets the embed ceiling of edge (g)'. It did. The survey deposit for ticket watchme-emits-a-probe refused whole at the host — cairn.devices.inference_domain.host.HostRefused: http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed refused (status 400): the input length exceeds the context length. The berth GATED and BERTHED fine; only the deposit refused, so the chain was unaffected (decompose template-filled from the FILE). What was lost is the survey tree's memory of the widest sweep yet run.

the_measurement.whole_rendering: survey_node_content(packet) = 16344 chars ~= 4405 tokens against nomic-embed-text's 2048 context — 2.15x over.
the_measurement.prior_survey_berths: 2001-6119 chars (539-1649 tok) — all under. Confirms the slate's read: the other faces have not been hit because their prose is shorter, not because they are bounded.
the_measurement.chars_per_token: 3.71, measured on real prose 2026-07-29; not re-derived here.
the_measurement.the_natural_grain_if_split: 46 parts (24 holdings + 11 sought + 10 absences + 1), largest 771 chars ~= 208 tokens, ZERO over the ceiling. The fix lands at ~10% of the ceiling, not a squeaker.

the_whole_chain_measured_2026-07-30.note: Measured AFTER the survey refusal, on the same ticket's chain (watchme-emits-a-probe). The first read — 'one face hit, one sweep's memory lost' — was WRONG and is corrected here.
the_whole_chain_measured_2026-07-30.decompose: 8730 chars — REFUSED, only 8% above what constrain passed at
the_whole_chain_measured_2026-07-30.triage_hypothesize_validate: PROJECTED to refuse (labeled a projection): each carries the 12 pieces' `what` strings VERBATIM plus its own additions, so all three exceed 8730.
the_whole_chain_measured_2026-07-30.the_real_bracket: The effective ceiling for THIS prose is between 8033 chars (passed) and 8730 chars (refused) — i.e. ~4.0-4.3 chars/token, HIGHER than the 3.71 measured on verdict prose on 2026-07-29. That figure under-predicts structured packet prose; do not carry it across faces as a constant. The honest bound is still the host's refusal.
the_whole_chain_measured_2026-07-30.the_structural_finding: This is not 'the prose got long'. The chain's VERBATIM-CARRY rule (each stage repeats the prior stage's strings byte-exact — the physics that makes the split adjudicable) guarantees the deposit rendering grows MONOTONICALLY with depth. So the LAST stages are the most likely to refuse, and validate — the berth the /sail entry gate reads — is the most exposed of all. Per-claim granularity is not an optimisation for this chain; it is the only shape that survives its own carry rule.

FINAL_TALLY_chain_complete.the_projection_was_WRONG_for_validate: I projected triage/hypothesize/validate would ALL refuse on the carry-rule argument. Triage and hypothesize did; VALIDATE DID NOT — 5397 chars, comfortably under. The reason matters: validate_node_content renders the CRITERIA (8 authored claims) and NOT the verbatim `covers` strings, so the carry rule does not reach its deposit rendering. The monotonic-growth argument holds only for faces whose node content re-renders the carried verbatim text — survey, decompose, triage and hypothesize do; validate does not. Correcting this rather than leaving the tidier generalisation standing: the growth is a property of each face's RENDERING, not of the chain's depth.
FINAL_TALLY_chain_complete.the_luckiest_fact: The one face the /sail entry gate READS (validate) is also the one late face that fits. If it had not, the gate would still have opened — it reads the berth FILE, not the tree — but the chain would have taught the trees nothing at all.

the_second_finding_which_matters_more: A VERDICT that fails to deposit is enqueued in ~/.cairn/devices/chart/verdict-deposits.jsonl and re-drained on the next door read (_learn calls _drain_before_serving first). A STAGE BERTH that fails to deposit is tracked by NOTHING — no ledger, no pending list, no re-drain. This one survived only because an operator was watching the terminal. That is Law 7's exact shape: loud at the diagnostic surface, ABSENT from the record of truth. It is also why every other face's edge-(g) hit would be silent, so it is the half to fix FIRST — the granularity fix without the ledger just makes the next silent loss less likely rather than visible.
the_settled_shape: Already proven once, on the verdict face 2026-07-29 (ticket a-node-holds-one-claim): verdict_node_parts renders one node per criterion verdict + one per hypothesis disposition, the whole rendering survives as a pure JOIN over those exact strings so the two renderings cannot drift, and deposit_verdict takes a METERED embed (embed_metered_via_domain) rather than a finished vector. Parts are bare of ticket/berth framing on purpose — node_id is a content hash, so attribution baked into content makes every part unique BY CONSTRUCTION, the property that makes a monolith undedupable; attribution rides provenance. The survey face's per-claim grain is already in its schema: {what,address} per holding, {what,measure} per absence, one string per sought. Same shape for the remaining five faces (constrain: one per constraint + per bound; decompose: one per sub_problem; triage: one per order entry; hypothesize: one per hypothesis; validate: one per criterion). It is a stone per face, NOT a sweep — the grain is per-face judgment.
disposition: At the close of watchme-emits-a-probe, cast ONE stone covering (1) the missing stage-berth deposit ledger — generalize the verdict ledger to any berth, since deposit_verdict/drain_pending already take nexus as a parameter — and (2) the survey face's per-claim granularity. Its live fire is ready-made: redeposit survey-20260730T112947-2317adecd700.json, an oversized specimen standing on disk. `live learn <berth>` is re-runnable and the tree's content-hash dedup makes a redeposit safe. The remaining five faces stay filed under edge (g) until their prose grows or their stone comes up. CORRECTED SCOPE 2026-07-30: the live fire is not one berth but EVERY refused berth of this voyage, plus the fix stone's own chart chain (which will hit the same wall while building the fix — the recursion is the sharpest possible live fire). Nothing is lost meanwhile: every berth stands on disk and `live learn <berth>` is re-runnable against content-hash dedup, so the cost is DEFERRED, not lost. That is why the running voyage was not parked.
what_was_deliberately_NOT_done: The berth was NOT trimmed to fit. It is a record of truth and Law 7 forbids editing one in place to make a downstream seam comfortable — the same discipline that produced the 2026-07-29 finding that the close mechanism had been quietly ratcheting an operator's prose budget.
laws_traced: Law 7 — the deposit refusal is loud at the terminal and absent from every record; that gap is the finding.
Law 3 — the ceiling was folklore for weeks; both numbers here are measured, and the parts-grain number was measured against this specific berth rather than estimated.
Law 1 — the fix is not a new design; the verdict face settled it and the other faces re-derive nothing.
